findings.title: The breaker trips on the same frame the load goes over: the cause is never seen, and an instant trip at 1.1x is false
findings.problem:
The load-budget beat is the only electricity in Big Meeting, and its key moment can't be read.

What happens:
- The gauge needle is set to draw/limit*0.9, or to 1 while tripped (src/meeting-strip.ts:84).
- Circuit.tick trips the source in the same tick the total passes the limit (src/sim/electrical.ts:46).
- So the needle's last live reading is 4.5 A / 5 A = 0.81, in the yellow (shot 25).
- Pressing E at the projector then jumps the needle straight to pinned red (shots 07, 23).

The player never sees 5.5 A sitting past the limit (the cause) before the CLACK (the effect). The switch press is the only visible cause, so 'loads add up until they pass the limit' becomes 'the projector switch breaks the strip'.

It is also false at the level taught. 5.5 A on 5 A is a 1.1x overload. Real thermal-magnetic breakers follow an inverse-time curve. Miniature UL 489 breakers must not trip at about 105% of rating, and must trip at 135% within about an hour:
- Schneider UL 489 calibration FAQ: https://www.se.com/us/en/faqs/FA98008
- Altech UL 489 datasheet: https://wolfautomation.com/content/altech-1pole-489-ctrip-datasheet.pdf

The game teaches that a strip trips the instant it is 0.01 A over. This confirms research leads M-2 and E-1.
findings.fix:
Give the strip a short, visible overload dwell before it trips:
1. Add an accumulator to Source (or keep it local to MeetingStrip): acc += max(0,(I/limit)^2 - 1)*dt.
2. Trip at acc >= 0.5, which is about 2.4 s at 1.1x. Also trip instantly when I > 3*limit.
3. During the dwell:
   - map the needle to min(1.15, I/limit)*0.87 so it visibly sits past the red line;
   - play a rising hum (audio.tone 90-140 Hz);
   - jitter the strip mesh and flicker the kettle and heater glows.
4. Then CLACK.
5. Add a DR-36 comment: 'real breakers trip in minutes at 1.1x; compressed to about 2 s as game tuning'.
6. Update src/sim/electrical.test.ts and tests/routes.spec.ts switchProjector (src/routes.spec lines 15-19), which waits 0.3 s: wait 3 s instead.
findings.verify: New unit test: 5.5 A on a 5 A source has not tripped after 1 s and has tripped by 3 s. Retake meeting-teach-07 at +1.0 s after the switch: the needle sits past the red line with Pip in frame. The routes.spec meeting tests still pass.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced frame by frame (v1.mjs A). On the first 1/60 s tick after E at the projector, the snapshot shows draw 5.5 and tripped:true together. On the next tick draw is 0. electrical.ts:46 trips in the same tick the total passes source.limit+1e-6, and meeting-strip.ts:84 pins the needle at 1 while tripped, so 5.5 A past the line is never drawn. Before the press the needle sits at 4.5/5*0.9=0.81 in the yellow (meeting-teach-25 crop). An instant trip at 1.1x is not how a thermal breaker behaves. Two citation problems: the cited 'research leads M-2 and E-1' do not exist in mockups/review5/research-external.md, and the test path is written as 'src/routes.spec' when it is tests/routes.spec.ts:15-16.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-meeting-teach/v1.mjs (scenario A frame log: frame0 draw 5.5 tripped true; frame1 draw 0)
findings.fix_correction: Do NOT add the accumulator to every Source in src/sim/electrical.ts. Lunch uses the same Circuit, two 5 A sources: lunch-runtime.ts:43-47 gives the lift a 9 A kick for 1 s and the conveyor a 3 A kick, and electrical.test.ts:8 and :10 ('lift kick trips unless…', 'reverse order trips') depend on brief overloads tripping straight away. A global I²t dwell of acc>=0.5 would stop the short, small overload in the reverse-order case from tripping and break the capacitor lesson. Make it opt-in instead: add an optional Source field (e.g. thermal?:{acc:number;trip:number;instant:number}) that only MeetingStrip sets (meeting-strip.ts:29). Keep instant tripping for sources without it, and keep the DR-36 comment next to it. Unit tests: 5.5 A on the thermal source has not tripped at 1 s and has tripped by 3 s; the existing Lunch tests still pass unchanged. routes.spec.ts:16 wait goes from .3 to about 3 s.

findings.title: While tripped, the gauge reads full-scale with zero current flowing, so unplugging shows no effect
findings.problem:
meeting-strip.ts:84 sets gauge.set(tripped ? 1 : draw/limit*.9). Once the breaker trips, the circuit draw is 0 A, but the needle is pinned at maximum (shots 13 and 23). A needle is a meter, so this teaches 'a tripped strip has the most current'.

It also kills the one moment where the player could watch cause and effect. In shot 13, unplugging the kettle while tripped leaves the needle exactly where it was. The player gets no evidence that removing a load lowered the total, until reset happens to work. Real load meters read zero when the breaker is open.
findings.fix:
Split the meter from the trip flag:
1. While tripped, drop the needle to 0 and show a separate red TRIPPED flag on the gauge face. Add a flag param to Gauge, or a lit red lamp on the strip next to the reset cap.
2. Add a faint ghost needle (a second line in Gauge.set at 35% alpha) for the demand the strip would carry if reset: the sum of the steady draws of the plugged and enabled loads, computed in MeetingStrip.render.
3. Unplugging the kettle while tripped then visibly drops the ghost needle from 5.5 to 3 A, below the red line. That is the cause-and-effect image the lesson needs.
findings.verify: Snapshot test: when tripped, the gauge value is 0 and the ghost value is 1.1. After unplugging the kettle, the ghost value is 0.6. Retake meeting-teach-13 and the gauge crop: the ghost needle moves out of the red.
findings.verify_reason: meeting-strip.ts:84 is gauge.set(tripped?1:draw/limit*.9). My run unplugged the kettle while tripped. The snapshot then showed draw 0 with tripped true, and the close-up shows the needle still pinned at the right end of the red. Unplugging a load while tripped therefore gives no feedback on the only meter. The ghost-needle idea is sound: draw is 0 while tripped (electrical.ts:35 skips loads on a tripped source), so the would-be demand has to be summed from the enabled, plugged loads' steady values in MeetingStrip.
findings.fix_correction: Gauge.set takes only a 0..1 value (kit.ts:103), so the ghost needle and the TRIPPED flag need a second parameter or a second draw pass in Gauge. Note that the shared Gauge is also used by Lunch (lunch-runtime.ts:60), so keep the new parameter optional.

findings.title: The load gauge has no units, labels or per-appliance share, so the player can't reason about which load to remove
findings.problem:
The only instrument is a three-zone arc with one needle. It has no number, no '5 A max' mark, no strip icon and nothing tying it to the kettle and heater (shots 04, 25).

- The code comment says it shows load 'in the same units as the cart gauges in Lunch Rush' (src/meeting-strip.ts:5-7), but there are no units anywhere.
- Nothing on the kettle, heater or projector says how much each draws, so 2.5 > 2 > 1 is invisible.
- The choice of what to unplug is fake. Kettle (2.5) or heater (2) alone each fixes the 0.5 A overload, so the player never compares sizes.
- 'Each appliance takes a share of one limit' is told by a single needle that most players won't link to the strip. It sits in the doorway above the strip, 1 m to the side.

This breaks DR-32: an abstract unit with no real-world tie. It also breaks DR-26: the concept is barely the mechanic, because the player unplugs whatever the prompt names.
findings.fix:
Make the share visible on the device:
1. Replace the arc with a stacked load bar on the strip's own housing, or mounted beside it. Each plugged appliance adds a coloured segment with its icon (kettle, heater, projector) and a length proportional to its draw. A thick ink line marks the limit, with a '5 A' plaque (or 'max 1150 W').
2. Give each appliance a small rating-plate decal ('2.5 A', '2 A', '1 A', or watts) visible at zoom 9.
3. Make the choice matter. Add a phone charger (0.2 A) on the strip, and set the projector to 1.2 A, so that unplugging the charger is not enough. The player then has to compare sizes.
4. Update the comment at meeting-strip.ts:5-7.
findings.verify: Close-up and game-camera shots of the strip: three segments read without the HUD, and the limit line is legible (14 px or more). New spec: unplug only the charger, reset, and the strip trips again.
findings.verify_reason: Gauge (kit.ts:100-108) draws only coloured arcs, a needle and a hub: no text, units or limit mark. Lunch's supply gauges use the same unlabelled Gauge() (lunch-runtime.ts:60), so the 'same units' comment at meeting-strip.ts:5-7 points at nothing. The appliances have no rating plates (meeting-strip.ts:35-45). Removing either load fixes the overload: 2.5+2+1=5.5, minus 2.5 is 3, minus 2 is 3.5. My run B unplugged one appliance and won with 0 trips. The fix arithmetic holds: with a 0.2 A charger and a 1.2 A projector the total is 5.9 A, removing only the charger leaves 5.7 A (still over), and removing the heater leaves 3.9 A.

findings.title: The fix can be found by following prompts (Reset, retrip, wander, 'Unplug the kettle'), and predicting the overload earns nothing
findings.problem:
The trip is effectively mandatory, and the recovery is prompt-driven.

At the switch, the prompt immediately offers 'E Reset the strip' (shot 07; promptFor gives the strip priority, src/ui/objectives.ts:66). Resetting while still overloaded trips again (my run: trips 2, shot 11). The player then wanders until the proximity prompt says 'E Unplug the kettle' (shot 12, meeting-strip.ts:73-77). That prompt names the fix, and the player can win without forming the idea 'too much on one strip'.

The player who reads the gauge does get somewhere: I verified that unplugging the heater before switching on wins with 0 trips (fail.mjs run C, 'preempt'). But nothing rewards that:
- The bonuses are deadline, damage and coffee (objectives.ts:33-36).
- Trips cost no damage or cost (win card, shot 15: 0 / 0, all A).
- Making coworkers groan costs nothing.

Lunch has a 'Never trip a breaker' bonus; Meeting, which is where the idea is introduced, does not.
findings.fix:
1. Replace 'Break fewer than 5 things' with 'Don't trip the strip' (ok: g.strip.trips===0). Damage already has its own grade axis.
2. Show 'Strip trips: N' on the result card (src/ui/game-ui.ts won()).
3. Make the appliance prompt describe, not instruct. Near an appliance while tripped, show 'E Unplug' with no noun until the player has looked at the gauge, or drop the proximity prompt for appliances entirely and keep the grab cue.
4. Add a real apply-the-idea option: a second wall socket inside the boardroom, at about (14.5,-3.2), on a separate circuit. Moving the heater's plug there (E to pick up the cord end, E at the socket) balances the load, and nobody groans. Bonus 'Nobody loses their tea or heat'. This teaches spreading loads across circuits, which is the real-world rule.
findings.verify: New spec: unplug the heater, then switch on, and the 'Don't trip the strip' star is lit. Spec: move the heater to the boardroom socket, and the job is won with unplugged===0 and trips===0. Result-card screenshot shows the trip count.
findings.verify_reason: Facts check out. The bonuses at objectives.ts:33-36 have no trip axis, while Lunch has 'Never trip a breaker' (objectives.ts:51). I reproduced the preemptive path (run B: unplug first, then switch on), which wins with trips 0, and its result card lists the same three bonuses with no trip count. The proximity prompt names the fix ('E Unplug the kettle', meeting-strip.ts:75-76). The priority is too high, though. The trip-then-unplug-and-reset loop is the designed lesson beat (review4 DESIGN_B.md:245; routes.spec.ts:12-14 comment), so a mandatory trip is intended. What remains is a grading and teaching polish gap: prediction earns nothing. That does not noticeably break play or understanding on its own, given findings 0, 1 and 2.
findings.fix_correction: Do not drop the appliance proximity prompt or replace it with a bare 'E Unplug'. DR-19 and the forgiving-interaction rule want a prompt that states the real action, and the prompt names the object, not a part value, so it does not breach DR-39 (which covers the card). Keep the prompt and put the teaching load on the gauge and the toast fixes. Replacing 'Break fewer than 5 things' with 'Don't trip the strip' is fine. The second-socket idea is optional scope, not required.

findings.title: REGRESSION-CHECK M11 still open: after the trip, the card and marker still say 'Switch the projector on' and point at the projector
findings.problem:
After the trip, the card reads 'Switch the projector on in the boardroom' (shots 07, 08, 11, 13, 21), but the player has just done exactly that. The bouncing marker stays over the projector (step at objectives.ts:32), not over the strip that needs attention.

The card isn't wrong (the projector isn't running), but it contradicts what the player sees and gives no direction. The strip's cue (a small red reset ball, 0.07 m radius, meeting-strip.ts:53 and :89) sits under Pip at the default camera (shot 07).

In run B, with the projector switched on early, plugging in trips the strip at once. The card jumps from step 2 straight to 'Switch the projector on', which the player already did (shot 21). This breaks DR-42: the card and marker must point at the current step's object.
findings.fix:
In JOBS.meeting step 3:
- set text to 'Get the projector running' (goal, not method);
- set at to g => g.strip?.tripped ? g.level.target : g.level.switchAt, so the marker hops to the strip while tripped.

Optionally insert a transient step while tripped, with text 'The strip has cut out', and render it in the card's flash style. Keep the text a 'what', not a 'how'.
findings.verify: tests/objectives.spec.ts: after the trip, the marker position equals the strip target (expose marker.position in the snapshot). Retake meeting-teach-08: the marker is over the strip.
findings.verify_reason: The problem is real: after the trip the card still reads 'Switch the projector on in the boardroom' (verify-03, verify-04, meeting-teach-08, meeting-teach-13). Step 3's at() is g.level.switchAt (objectives.ts:32), so the marker stays over the projector while the prompt pill says 'Reset the strip'. The card and the prompt disagree, which breaks DR-42. The 'REGRESSION-CHECK M11' label is wrong, however. M11 in research-external.md:113 is the 'voltage flows' wording misconception, and no earlier review (review3, review4) raised this card issue. Treat it as a new finding, not a regression.
findings.fix_correction: Fine as written. Use the strip's live position, not g.level.target: MeetingStrip.stripAt() is private, so either expose it or use prop(g,'strip')??g.level.target in the step's at(). g.strip.tripped is the public getter (meeting-strip.ts:61).

findings.title: The trip has no in-world cause cue at the faulty part and no sentence naming the cause
findings.problem:
The trip effects (meeting-strip.ts:82) are:
- 14 small yellow sparks at y 0.3, 4 dust puffs and a 0.12 shake at the strip;
- the kettle and heater glows go out.

At the default camera, Pip stands between the camera and the strip (Pip at z -3.2, strip at z -1.95, camera behind Pip). The sparks are almost fully hidden (shot 07, +0.15 s), and by +1 s the frame shows no failure at all (shot 08).

No toast or sentence ever names the cause, which DR-28 requires: a world cue at the faulty part, then one sentence naming the physical cause. The appliances going dark is a good cue, but it reads as 'the power went', not 'too much on one strip'.

Resetting while overloaded (trip 2) gets identical feedback, so the player learns nothing new from the second failure.
findings.fix:
1. Turn the camera toward the strip at the trip for about 0.6 s: a lookAt bias on game.yaw, as the win push-in does (game.ts:373).
2. Add a puff of smoke from the strip and a 'thunk' of the boardroom lights dimming (pendant glow off for 0.3 s).
3. On the first trip, show one toast naming the cause, not the fix: 'Strip overloaded: everything plugged into it adds up past its limit.'
4. On a repeat trip after a reset with no load removed: 'Still too much on the strip.'
5. Reuse the station toast element (shared.ts), and fade it after 4 s (DR-40).
findings.verify: Retake shots at +0.1, +0.5 and +1.0 s after the switch: the strip is unoccluded, smoke is visible and the toast text is present. Spec: the second trip shows the second message.
findings.verify_reason: meeting-strip.ts:82 emits 14 sparks and 4 dust at y 0.3 at the strip, plus a 0.12 shake. In my shot at +0.13 s at the default camera (verify-03) no sparks can be made out: Pip stands over the strip, and the only cues are the appliances going dark and a small red reset cap. meeting-strip.ts and game.ts contain no toast or sentence naming the cause, and a repeat trip gives identical feedback. DR-28 is not met.
findings.fix_correction: Drop step 1 (auto-turning game.yaw toward the strip at the trip). The hard rule requires a player-controlled orbit camera, and the win push-in at game.ts:373 is an end-of-level exception, not a mid-play one. Make the cue visible from the player's own camera instead: emit the burst and a smoke column at y 0.8-1.4 so it clears Pip's silhouette, pop up a tall red breaker flag on the strip, and dim the boardroom pendants. Keep the one-sentence cause toast (under 25 words, fading after 4 s per DR-40) and the second-trip variant.

findings.title: Current pulses don't match the circuit: none on the reel while it feeds the kettle and heater; idle hint dots flow on an open circuit
findings.problem:
Pulses are drawn only when loads[0] (the projector) is on: game.ts:305 calls pulses.update(..., this.circuit.loads[0].state==='on').

- After plug-in the reel carries 4.5 A to the kettle and heater (snapshot draw 4.5), yet it is plain gold with no pulses (shots 03, 24).
- The kettle and heater cords (meeting-strip.ts:94-96) never show flow.
- So the room teaches that current flows only when the 'target' device is on. It also hides the point that the reel is already carrying most of the strip's budget.

Separately, re-checking known DR-29: the 40-dot cyan idle hint (game.ts:101, :446-447) still flows from Pip toward the door at 40 s, with nothing plugged in (shot 20). That contradicts 'dots mean current' on the same floor.
findings.fix:
1. Drive reel pulses from the strip draw: (this.circuit.draw.get('reel')??0)>0, with density or speed scaled to draw/limit.
2. Draw pulses on each appliance cord while its load is on. Reuse Pulses with the cord's TubeGeometry curve.
3. Replace the idle hint dots with static, non-glowing chevrons painted along the route, or footprints. That keeps moving dots reserved for current.
findings.verify: After plug-in, the snapshot reports pulses visible on the reel (expose pulses.visible). A crop shows beads on the reel and the cords before the projector is on. An idle shot at 40 s shows no moving emissive dots.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:305 passes this.circuit.loads[0].state==='on' (loads[0] is the projector, game.ts:102) as the pulses' visible flag. After plug-in the snapshot shows strip draw 4.5 with the kettle and heater 'on', yet the reel is plain gold with no beads (verify-02). Appliance cords are plain TubeGeometry with no flow (meeting-strip.ts:94-96). The idle hint (game.ts:100-101, 446-447) shows cyan dots after 35 s with nothing connected (meeting-teach-20: 'Pick up the plug' prompt, dots in front of Pip). Both break DR-29.

findings.title: Power flows the wrong way through the connectors: Pip pushes the live male plug from the closet into the strip's sockets (a 'suicide cord')
findings.problem:
The reel is anchored at the closet outlet (meeting.ts:33, anchor -11.4,-7.8), and Pip carries its free end.

- That end is modelled as a male plug: the plug and coupler prefab is a body plus two brass pins (src/props/prefabs.ts:101-102); game.ts:86 uses it as this.plug. The action-bar icon is a pronged plug, and the prompts say 'Pick up the plug' and 'Plug in' (shots 01, 30).
- The free end of a cable that is live from the wall would then have energised, exposed pins. That is the male-to-male 'suicide cord' the CPSC warns against: https://abc7news.com/post/federal-safety-agency-warns-not-use-male-double-pronged-extension-cords-due-risk-electrocution-fire/18907805/ and https://acworks.com/blogs/ac-works-connector/the-dangers-of-double-male-ended-cords.
- The strip is a distributor (it feeds the kettle and heater), yet it is fed through one of its own outlets (strip sockets, prefabs.ts:138). That is backwards: a strip is fed by its own plug.

At the level taught (source to cable to strip to loads), the connector genders show the direction of supply, and this teaches it reversed. It applies to the Playground lamp socket too.
findings.fix:
Make the hand-held end a socket.
1. Add a 'connector' render of the free end in prefabs.ts: an orange box with a slotted face and no pins.
2. Give the strip a short stub lead ending in a plug (prefabs.ts:138).
3. On snap (game.ts:205), seat the strip's plug into the connector with the existing plugFlash.
4. Keep the verbs, but word the prompts truthfully: 'Pick up the cable end', 'Connect the strip'.
5. Alternative with the same geometry: move the reel drum, with its sockets, to the boardroom side, and have Pip walk the plug back to the closet outlet. That matches how real reels are used.
6. Do the same in the Playground: put a plug on the lamp's lead.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 shots of the carried cable end (no pins) and of the seated strip (strip plug in the connector). The objectives specs still pass with the renamed prompts.
findings.verify_reason: The core claim checks out in code. The carried end is makeProp('coupler') (game.ts:86), and the coupler/plug prefab is a body plus two brass pins (prefabs.ts:101-102). The reel is anchored at the closet outlet (meeting.ts:33), so the free end carries live pins, which is reversed from real reel use. One detail is wrong: the strip is not fed through one of its own outlets. The plug seats into a separate dark 'socket' box at the target (game.ts:88, 205), which sits beside the strip (strip at target z+0.3, game.ts:211). Priority is too high. Connector gender and supply direction are not what Big Meeting teaches (its lesson is the load budget). At game zoom the pins barely read (meeting-teach-30 shows a yellow cylinder in Pip's hand). This is a truthfulness polish item, not a noticeable teaching hit.
findings.fix_correction: Fix the evidence: the receptacle is the dark socket box at game.ts:88, not the strip's sockets at prefabs.ts:138. The lighter fix is to make the carried end a female connector (no pins, slotted face) and turn the game.ts:88 box into the strip's own short plug lead. Moving the reel drum to the boardroom would change the cable-length and strain design of every cable floor, so treat it as out of scope.

findings.title: After plug-in the prompt offers 'Grab the power strip', and lifting it silently cuts power while the plug stays 'in' on the floor
findings.fix:
Lock the strip once the reel is plugged in:
1. Exclude the strip from nearest() while g.connected && stripPlaced(), and keep it Fixed.
2. If it is grabbed some other way, disconnect explicitly: connected=false, holdingPlug stays false, a plug pop sound, and the plug drops 0.3 m from the strip.
3. The first-step prompt then shows nothing, or 'Tab to look around'.
findings.verify: Spec: after plug-in, the prompt does not contain 'Grab the power strip', and E at the strip leaves stripPlaced true. Retake meeting-teach-04 with no grab prompt.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced (v1.mjs B). Right after plug-in, standing at the strip, the prompt is 'E Grab the power strip' (also verify-02, meeting-teach-26). E lifts it: held 'strip', stripPlaced false, draw 0, the appliances go 'off', and the cable stays connected (meeting-teach-27). Setting it down restores draw 4.5 with no plug action. The prompt is truthful (E does grab the strip), so DR-19 is not strictly broken. The real problem is DR-42: the prompt competes with the current step's object. It is fully recoverable with one more E, so P2 rather than P1.
findings.fix_correction: Excluding the strip from nearest() after plug-in is right. Also check the plug-pickup branch at game.ts:219, which unplugs the reel when E is pressed within 1.75 m of plugPosition and no closer prop is found. Once the strip is excluded, E at the strip would unplug the cable instead, which is the same problem in a new form. Either gate that branch for the meeting while stripPlaced, or require F for unplugging.

findings.title: The load gauge floats in the open boardroom doorway, with a bare black slab back
findings.problem:
The gauge is mounted at (t.x+0.95, 1.55, t.z+0.06), which is (13.25, 1.55, -2.19) (meeting-strip.ts:52).

- That is inside the door gap, which runs x 11 to 13.8 (decor.ts:144-145; LEVEL_01 says the same). There is no wall or post behind it, so it hangs in mid-air.
- From inside the boardroom it reads as a black rectangle floating in the doorway (shots 05, 09).
- Seen from the open plan, it hovers among the chairs behind the glass line (shots 03, 13).
- It is the room's only teaching instrument, and it looks like a stray decal rather than part of the strip.
findings.fix:
Mount the gauge on something solid. Choose one:
- the glass pane's metal post at x 13.8, with the gauge at x 14.3, z -1.96, facing +z;
- better, a small post on the strip's own base (with the stacked bar from the gauge-units finding), so the instrument visibly belongs to the strip.

Give the back a housing (rbox with a bevel, not a flat INK box).
findings.verify: Orbit shots at 0/90/180/270 degrees at zoom 9: the gauge always sits on a mount. Check the gauge position against the door-gap bounds.
findings.verify_reason: The gauge mount is at t.x+.95=13.25, z -2.19 (meeting-strip.ts:52; target 12.3,-2.25 at meeting.ts:33). That is inside the door gap, x 11 to 13.8, at z -2 (decor.ts:144-146; the post is at x 13.8). Gauge.mount builds only a flat INK box plus a decal (kit.ts:108): no housing and no support. meeting-teach-05 shows the bare black slab floating in the doorway. This breaks DR-72 and DR-63.

findings.title: Appliance prompts pick the first match in array order, so the heater is hard to target
findings.problem:
interact() and prompt() use this.appliances.find(x=>dist<1.3) (meeting-strip.ts:66, :75), not the nearest appliance.

The kettle (13.95,-1.62) and heater (15.15,-1.68) are 1.2 m apart. Standing right at the heater front, about (15.15,-1.2), is 1.27 m from the kettle, so the prompt still says 'Unplug the kettle'. At (14.6,-0.9) my run also got the kettle (fail.mjs C).

If the choice of load ever matters (the gauge-units fix), the player can't select the one they reasoned about.
findings.fix: Pick the nearest appliance within 1.0 m: sort by dist, take [0]. Show the grab-cue reticle on that appliance's cord end.
findings.verify: Spec: walk to (15.2,-1.15), and the prompt contains 'heater'; at (13.9,-1.15) it contains 'kettle'.
findings.verify_reason: Stronger than reported. meeting-strip.ts:66 and :75 use find() in array order (kettle first). In run B I walked to the heater's front: Pip ended at (15.02,-1.00), (14.75,-1.01) and (14.97,-1.17), 0.6-0.7 m from the heater, and every position prompted 'E Unplug the kettle', because the kettle is still within 1.3 m (for example 1.24 m at (15.02,-1.00)). Pressing E unplugged the kettle. The heater is effectively only selectable from its far right side.

findings.title: A kettle 'left on' draws power forever, and its 'on' state is a big white fog ball
findings.problem:
The room claims the kettle is 'left on, as office kettles are' (meeting-strip.ts:2-3), and it draws 2.5 A steadily. Real kettles switch themselves off when the water boils, using a steam-triggered bimetal: Ingenia, https://www.ingenia.org.uk/articles/how-do-kettles-know-when-to-switch-off. A permanently drawing kettle is a wrong mental model, and it makes the 'unplug the kettle' answer arbitrary.

The kettle's 'on' cue is a white glow sprite, scale 0.6, at 1.25 m (meeting-strip.ts:47). It renders as a large translucent white sphere beside the gauge (shots 04, 25), which reads as fog, not a working appliance.
findings.fix:
Swap the kettle for a hot-water urn, which sits on its thermostat all day (reuse the cyl body, taller, with a tap). Or keep the kettle and make it re-boil in a cycle: kick 2.5 A for 8 s, then 0 for 6 s, a nice 'it only trips when the kettle comes on' beat.

Replace the white halo with:
- the existing steam puffs (already at :92);
- a small red lit lamp on the appliance's switch.

Keep the heater's orange grille.
findings.verify: A close-up shows no white halo sphere, and the urn's or kettle's lit lamp reads at zoom 9. Update the comment at meeting-strip.ts:2-3.
findings.verify_reason: The kettle is a constant 2.5 A steady load with no cycling (meeting-strip.ts:19, 32), and the header claims office kettles are left on (lines 1-2). Real kettles cut out at the boil. The 'on' cue is a white glow sprite, scale 0.6, at y 1.25 (meeting-strip.ts:47) at opacity 0.35-0.45, and it renders as a large translucent white disc over the doorway (verify-02 upper right, meeting-teach-05 left, meeting-teach-25).

findings.title: The projector's switch state is invisible; switched on early, the trip lands on the cable plug-in
findings.problem:
The 'switch' is a 1.9 m radius around the projector on the table (game.ts:244, :217). It has no rocker and no standby LED. A press gives only a 6-spark burst and the prompt word changing ('Switch it on' or 'Switch it off', objectives.ts:77).

If the player switches on before plugging in, which the prompt allows ('Switch on (needs power first)'), the strip trips at the instant the cable goes in (run B, shot 21). The player will blame the cable or the plug, not the total load.

After the trip, nothing on the projector shows it is still switched on. Yet that latent 'on' is why a reset re-trips (shot 11).
findings.fix:
1. Add a rocker on the projector housing (decor.ts:149) that tilts with game.switchedOn.
2. Add an LED: amber when on but unpowered, green when running, off when off.
3. With the trip dwell from the first finding, a plug-in into an already-on projector hums for about 2 s first, so the needle is seen climbing past the line.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 projector shots in the off, on-unpowered and running states, readable without the HUD.
findings.verify_reason: The projector is an rbox plus a lens cylinder (decor.ts:149), with no rocker or LED. The switch toggles game.switchedOn with only a 6-spark burst and a tone (game.ts:217). Switched on before plug-in, closing the lead trips the strip on the next tick (game.ts:348 sets loads[0].enabled from switchedOn), as meeting-teach-21 shows: 'Reset the strip' right at plug-in.

findings.title: The tidy route is a daisy chain (wall, reel, coupler, reel, strip), which real safety guidance forbids, and the room never frames it
findings.problem:
The intended clean solution (tests/routes.spec.ts:38-45, LEVEL_01 'Clean') joins two extension reels with a coupler, then feeds a power strip from them.

Office safety guidance from ESFI and OSHA says strips plug directly into the wall and cords are not chained. Chaining violates 29 CFR 1910.303(b)(2) as typically applied: https://ehs.okstate.edu/site-files/documents/daisy_chaining_factsheet.pdf and https://www.ocwr.gov/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/fastfacts_power_strips.pdf.

A game that teaches electricity truthfully shouldn't present the forbidden setup as the 'tidy' answer without comment. The coupler is also the same model as the plug (prefabs.ts:101), so it doesn't read as a rated joiner.
findings.fix:
Reframe the parts so the clean route is a legitimate setup:
- Make the second reel a single long heavy-duty site cable.
- Make the 'coupler' a rated inline connector with a visible rating plate.
- Make the strip a rated 'distribution box' (a real thing on sites), so the setup reads as wall, heavy lead, distribution box, appliances.

At minimum, add a DR-36 comment in meeting.ts. Never put the Lunch thin-cable lesson on chained leads.
findings.verify: Close-up of the coupler and distribution box showing a rating plate. Code check: the comment exists.
findings.verify_reason: routes.spec.ts:38-45 and LEVEL_01:20 make the clean route reel + coupler + second reel, then the strip. The coupler and the plug share one model (prefabs.ts:101 'case coupler: case plug'). meeting.ts has no DR-36 comment framing it. Daisy-chaining extension leads and strips does go against common office safety guidance. I did not open the external URLs; that claim is consistent with general knowledge.

findings.title: The design doc and code comments misdescribe the lesson (26 m reel, no load beat, 'same units' that don't exist)
findings.problem:
docs/LEVEL_01_BIG_MEETING.md never mentions the load-budget beat, the kettle, the heater, the strip breaker or the gauge. It still gives the reel as 26 m (:16, code: 23.2), and its acceptance criterion is 'No text needed' (:30).

src/meeting-strip.ts:5-7 claims the gauge uses the same units as Lunch's cart gauges, but neither is labelled. Future fixers will tune against the wrong intent.
findings.fix:
Update LEVEL_01:
- add a 'Lesson: load budget' section covering the appliances, draws, strip limit, the trip-dwell rule, the unplug and spread-load solutions and the bonus;
- set the reel to 23.2 m and the coupled length to 37.2 m.

Rewrite the meeting-strip.ts header to match the shipped gauge.
findings.verify: Doc review against the snapshot values: draws 2.5/2/1, limit 5, reel maxLength 23.2 / 37.2.
findings.verify_reason: LEVEL_01_BIG_MEETING.md:16 says 26 m, but the code says length 23.2 (meeting.ts:33), and the extension adds 14 m for 37.2 m (game.ts attachNear: rope.maxLength=level.length+14). The doc never mentions the kettle, heater, strip breaker or gauge, and :30 says 'No text needed'. The 'same units as the Lunch cart gauges' comment (meeting-strip.ts:5-7) refers to equally unlabelled gauges (lunch-runtime.ts:60).

notes.playability:
The full clean solve (strip, reel, coupler and second reel via F at the cart, plug, switch, trip, unplug, reset) worked through the capture helper in about 33 s of game time, with no console errors in any of 3 runs. The early-switch path and the pre-emptive-unplug path also complete.

Playability issues:
- the appliance prompt picks by array order (the heater is hard to select);
- the strip can be lifted after plug-in.

I found no soft-locks in the load beat: a reset is always available, and replugging appliances toggles freely.
notes.fun: The trip is a decent comedy beat: groans, '!' bubbles in the boardroom (shot 14) and appliances dying. But it lands mostly off-camera, and it is over in one frame, so the 'hum, then CLACK' drama is lost. A 2 s rising hum with a buzzing strip and flickering kettle would make it both funnier and truthful. Choosing who loses their tea (or moving the heater to another circuit to avoid the groan) would give the player a small, readable decision instead of an obligatory toggle.
